title: Largest sum-free set of quadratic residues
statement: For a prime p let QR_p be the set of the (p-1)/2 nonzero squares modulo p. Let s(p) be the largest size of a subset A of QR_p that is sum-free: a + b = c (mod p) has no solution with a, b, c in A (a = b allowed). Determine s(p), and the behaviour of s(p) / |QR_p| as p grows. The headline cell is p = 1009: find a sum-free set of more than 174 quadratic residues modulo 1009.
submission: Text file: the elements of A, distinct nonzero squares modulo 1009 written as integers in 1..1008, separated by spaces or newlines.
score: the number of elements (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: a sum-free set of 174 quadratic residues found by randomized greedy construction with local search (tools/qr_sumfree_search.py)

context: Erdos showed that every set of n nonzero integers contains a sum-free subset of more than n/3 elements, Alon and Kleitman extended this to finite groups, and Eberhard, Green and Manners proved that the constant 1/3 cannot be improved; for subsets A of F_p* the largest sum-free subset sf(A) is at least |A|/3 + O(|A|/p), and sets for which sf(A) is close to |A|/3 must be evenly spread over the cosets of large multiplicative subgroups (arXiv:2004.01884). The quadratic residues, the most studied pseudo-random subset of F_p, are themselves a multiplicative subgroup, so s(p) asks where they sit between the general bound |QR_p|/3 and the trivial |QR_p|. The exact values below fluctuate (s(61) = 16 of 30, s(97) = 18 of 48, s(101) = 22 of 50), and our best set for p = 1009 is 174 of 504, close to one third; whether s(p)/|QR_p| tends to 1/3 is open.
references: P. Erdos, Extremal problems in number theory, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 8 (1965) 181-189
N. Alon, D. J. Kleitman, Sum-free subsets, in A Tribute to Paul Erdos (Cambridge University Press, 1990) 13-26
S. Eberhard, B. Green, F. Manners, Sets of integers with no large sum-free subset, Annals of Math. 180 (2014) 621-652

novelty.verdict: new as stated. The largest sum-free subset of a general set A is a classical function (Erdos; Alon and Kleitman); its value for A = the quadratic residues modulo p is not tabulated anywhere we found (OEIS, arXiv), and the sequence s(p) is not in the OEIS.
closest: The general sum-free subset problem sf(A) (Erdos 1965, Alon-Kleitman 1990, Eberhard-Green-Manners 2014) and its multiplicative-subgroup refinement (arXiv:2004.01884): this problem is the case A = QR_p, which no source evaluates.

first_values.note: Exact values for every prime p <= 113 by exhaustive branch and bound (each candidate residue checked against all sums of chosen ones); the p = 1009 value is our best known lower bound. Our heuristic reproduces every exact value it was tried on (p = 61, 101).

baseline.text: 174 for p = 1009, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the set in `refs/qr-sumfree.txt`. Lower bound from the general theory: at least |QR_p|/3 + O(|QR_p|/p), about 168; upper bound: trivially at most 504, and no better bound is proved here.
